pattern.description: The stack of inbox cards under 'Every email' drifts down and out of frame. Then the second word swaps: 'call' drops in from above while 'email' exits, so 'Every' stays put and the headline becomes 'Every call'.
pattern.why_premium: Keeping the anchor word fixed and swapping only the noun makes a list of data sources (email, call, ...) read as one sentence building up. Clearing the card stack first leaves room for the swap.

build_hint.gsap: tl.to('.card-stack .card', {y: 300, autoAlpha: 0, duration: 0.45, ease: 'power2.in', stagger: {each: 0.04, from: 'end'}}); tl.to('.swap-word.old', {y: 30, autoAlpha: 0, duration: 0.2, ease: 'power2.in'}, '-=0.15'); tl.fromTo('.swap-word.new', {y: -30, autoAlpha: 0}, {y: 0, autoAlpha: 1, duration: 0.25, ease: 'power3.out'}, '<0.05').
build_hint.remotion: Cards translateY = interpolate(frame, [0, 14], [0, 300], {easing: Easing.in(Easing.quad)}) with opacity 1->0; old word translateY 0->30 and opacity 1->0 over frames 16-21; new word spring({frame: frame - 18, fps, config: {damping: 200}}) mapping translateY -30->0 and opacity 0->1.

notes: input_text_cycle is used loosely: the cycling text is a headline word, not an input field (kinetic_word_reveal is the alternative). b02 overlaps the same text, so it is not used. b04 is a residual strip from the departing cards. Cards look like they slide down, but it could be a mask wipe. Clicks/ticks are visible at about 12.15, 12.25, 12.35 and 12.45 s on the spectrogram (likely music hits) but there are no SFX candidates.
